title: fix(clone): a cross-user `clone get --what buffer` names an older daemon, not the deny
description:
## the defect

since the clone auth gate reads the peer's pid (#678), a `clone get --what buffer` from another unix
user is refused by the gate: the server replies with a rejected ack,
`{ phase: 'rejected', reason: 'auth-denied' }`.

`asCloneGetReply` maps any ack that carries a `phase` to `peer-probe-blind` (the path for an older
daemon that predates the read channel). so the refused caller reads:

```
😶 @:<clone> — the buffer could not be read
   ├─ cause
   │  └─ peer-probe-blind
   └─ fix
      └─ this daemon predates the read channel — re-enroll the clone to a version that answers a probe
```

the security invariant holds: no row of the box reaches the caller. the copy names a false cause and
a false cure: a re-enroll cannot make another user's read pass.

## the shape of the fix

- in `asCloneGetReply`, read a rejected ack with `reason: 'auth-denied'` as the deny it is, before
  the older-daemon fallthrough
- either a new probe-blind reason (the closed set is `CLONE_PROBE_BLIND_REASONS`; each copy map is
  compiler-forced), or a classed throw on the get path that renders the same `auth-denied` reject
  copy `clone say` renders
- the say's baseline probe meets the same ack for a cross-user say, so the choice must keep that
  say refused at dispatch, exit 1, with its extant copy

## the pin

`blackbox/cli/clone.say.slowbox.realbrain.acceptance.test.ts` `[case2][t1]` snaps today's tree; the
fix moves that snapshot on purpose.

found in the 5.3 verification review of the #678 behavior.
